matches.rationale: No finding addresses the abstract's exaggerated claim that the results 'completely avoid memorization even in highly overparameterized settings.'
No finding identifies inconsistent stopping times across models biasing comparisons of memorization timings.
No finding mentions the inconsistency between sub-Gaussian bounded covariance assumptions and heavy-tailed/covariance mixtures.

Both describe cherry-picking of runs: GT4 says failed runs were removed without disclosure, artificially reducing variance; pred 5 identifies exclusion of runs where early stopping failed to improve FID by >15%, leading to biased, reduced-variance estimates.
No finding addresses promotional language in the conclusion overstating robustness and applicability.
No finding identifies the missing ethics/privacy statement in acknowledgments or appendix.
No finding mentions the fabricated reference [42] supporting architectural regularization claims.

Pred 3 finds an inverted formula error within the method section, but GT8 concerns a global narrative mismatch between the theoretical scaling τ_mem~ψ_n/Δ_t and experimental scaling claims lacking Δ_t dependence; these are distinct issues.
No finding discusses underestimated variance from bootstrap confidence intervals with only 1000 samples on memorization fraction.
No finding addresses the introduction's sweeping dismissal of prior work and exaggerated novelty claims.

Both highlight the logical incoherence in the 'memorization is not due to data repetition' paragraph: conflicting experimental results, flawed equality of sample presentations, and contradictory claims about the cause.
No finding discusses unstandardized training lengths across U-Net width comparisons confounding memorization-time scaling laws.
No finding mentions the lack of sensitivity analysis for the nearest-neighbor threshold k=1/3 and its potential to artificially enforce τ_mem scaling.
No finding identifies the conclusion's overgeneralization to all score-based models without sufficient evidence.
Both identify reference [12] as a fabricated or non-legitimate source: GT15 notes it is a future/unpublished work; pred 1 details placeholder author names and 'speculative report' status.
No finding addresses the oversimplified definition of generalization loss as L_test−L_train ignoring estimator bias/noise complexities.
